Andy Robertson believes that tightening up at the back will be central to giving Arne Slot the platform he needs to mount a serious Premier League title push in his debut campaign as Liverpool manager. The Scotland captain pointed out that, while the season is still in its infancy, Liverpool’s defensive record offers encouragement: they are yet to concede in their first two league fixtures. Those games, against Ipswich Town and Brentford, allowed Slot to begin his tenure with successive clean sheets and a sense of early momentum, but Robertson acknowledged that a far sterner examination lies ahead. Liverpool travel to Old Trafford on Sunday, and he expects Manchester United to pose a much more dangerous attacking threat, providing a more accurate indication of how far the team has progressed defensively under their new coach.

handle Robertson stressed that the focus within the squad is on building defensive consistency, not just enjoying a brief run of good results. Two clean sheets from two matches, he said, represent an ideal start and something that the players were eager to achieve, especially after last season’s frustrations. He made clear that Liverpool want to extend this run for as long as possible, beginning with restricting Manchester United to as few opportunities as they can. Beyond that, he said the aim after the forthcoming international break will be to limit chances for every opponent they face, turning solid defensive performances into a defining feature of their campaign rather than a short-lived phase. For Robertson, that requires collective effort: the backline, goalkeeper, and the rest of the team pressing from the front all have roles in cutting down the number of shots and clear openings Liverpool allow.

Looking back at the previous season, Robertson was candid about where Liverpool fell short. The club conceded 41 goals across their 38 league games, finishing third but shipping more goals than both Manchester City, who won the title, and Arsenal, who ended as runners-up. Liverpool let in seven more than City and 12 more than Arsenal, statistics that underline the defensive gap they must close if they are to seriously contend for the championship. Robertson observed that even during the period when Liverpool were firmly in the title race, underlying numbers showed they were giving up more chances than their two main rivals. In his view, when a team consistently allows opponents too many opportunities, it is only a matter of time before one match inflicts decisive damage on their ambitions—and he feels that is precisely what occurred last season. The defender’s message under Slot, therefore, is that Liverpool must transform early “promising signs” at the back into a sustained improvement over the entire campaign if they want to avoid being punished again at crucial moments.
